liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dark Star** (3 reviews): Reviewer finds this Dark Star interesting; Reviewer calls it a must-have Dark Star, with Garcia's playing ranging from very soft to very loud [12][13][16]
- **Hard To Handle** (2 reviews): Reviewer says this was the first time the band played Hard To Handle; Reviewer calls the first-ever Hard To Handle a mess [8][16]
- **The Eleven** (1 review): Reviewer's favorite part of the show; several Jerry lead passages stand out [12]

## Setlist highlights

- **William Tell Bridge**: rare: 5 archived performances [17]
- Earliest performances in the archive: Hard To Handle [17]

## The recordings

- **gd1969-03-15.140931.sbd.miller.sirmick.flac1644** (recommended): soundboard; 7 songs; 77 min; rated 2.67/5 by 3 [1]
- **gd69-03-15.sbd.kaplan.28798.sbeok.flacf**: soundboard; 7 songs; 76 min; rated 3/5 by 6 [2]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says the tape quality is modest, since the band played for dancers in the room, not for listeners; A cut around the 45-minute mark is presumably the cassette master being flipped [2][11]
- **gd69-03-15.sbd.cotsman.4280.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 6 songs; 68 min; rated 3.4/5 by 10 [4]. Said about its sound: Reviewer rates the recording four stars out of five and suggests using an equalizer; Significant hiss is present, and no noise reduction was applied; There is a splice near the start of The Eleven [4][13]
- **gd1969-03-15.176592.sbd.spc.bear.miller.sirmick.daniel.flac1644**: soundboard; 6 songs; 74 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [3]

## Around the show

- Pig Pen is heard on both vocals and organ during this performance [6]
- Per Deadbase, the performance was the Black & White Ball [8]
- Reviewer recalls the Ball as an annual high-society series of SF events, mostly opera and symphony, later adding rock acts [9]
- Reviewer doubts the Dead were ever invited back to the Ball [9]
- The Black & White Ball is a San Francisco Symphony fundraiser with formal white-tie and black-dress attire [10]
- The show was the Black and White Ball, a San Francisco Symphony benefit [1]
- Reviewer says the show doesn't match the Fillmore run but is still worth having [16]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1969-03-15.140931.sbd.miller.sirmick.flac1644**: taped by Bear; transferred by Charlie Miller and SIRMick; source: Source: SBD > Bear's cassette > ??? > Sony ESXHiFi/L-750 beta tape; Transfer: PCM (Sony SL-10) > Sony PCM-601ESD > Behringer Ultramatch Pro > Tascam DA-3000… [1]. Also: Minor dropouts were repaired, and one larger dropout was patched using shnid 28798 [1]
- **gd69-03-15.sbd.kaplan.28798.sbeok.flacf**: taped by Bear; transferred by Morgan and Seth Kaplan; source: Soundboard [2]. Also: The tape came from Bear's private tape collection; Sourced from Bear's cassette master, with lineage MSC>C>D>CD; The original tape ran a half step flat; pitch was corrected using Cool Edit 2000 [2][11]
- **gd69-03-15.sbd.cotsman.4280.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [4]. Also: This copy only partly covers the first set, lacking Dew, Alligator and drums that Deadbase places before Hard to Handle; Taken from a bootleg CD of unknown generations [4][8]
- **gd1969-03-15.176592.sbd.spc.bear.miller.sirmick.daniel.flac1644**: taped by Recorded by Owsley "Bear" Stanley; transferred by remastered by Daniel February 4th, 2026; source: SBD > Cassette > ? > PCM (Sony Beta L-750) [3]

## Art and photos

- Poster by pleasantdeadposter.com: [GRATEFUL DEAD 1969 Hilton Hotel Black & White Ball Concert Poster BILL GRAHAM](https://pleasantdeadposter.com/grateful-dead-1969-hilton-hotel-black-white-ball-concert-poster-bill-graham.htm) [18]
- Poster by pleasantdeadposter.com: [GRATEFUL DEAD 1969 Hilton Hotel Black & White Ball Concert Poster BILL GRAHAM](https://pleasantdeadposter.com/grateful-dead-1969-hilton-hotel-black-white-ball-concert-poster-bill-graham.htm) [19]
